Heritage sites by state

Heritage sites in Tamil Nadu: Chola temples, Mahabalipuram and Gingee

Tamil Nadu shares in five UNESCO listings: the Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram, the Great Living Chola Temples (Thanjavur, Gangaikonda Cholapuram, Darasuram), Gingee Fort within the Maratha Military Landscapes, the Nilgiri Mountain Railway and the natural Western Ghats. Add Madurai, Kanchipuram, Srirangam and Chidambaram, and the excavated sites of Keeladi, Adichanallur and Arikamedu.

Our South India temple architecture tour covers Mahabalipuram, Kanchipuram and the Chola temples, and we also arrange single-day visits for groups.

Why Tamil Nadu is India's temple heartland

Tamil Nadu has the longest unbroken temple tradition in India. Pallava kings at Kanchipuram and Mahabalipuram carved rock-cut shrines and built the first large structural temples in stone in the 7th and 8th centuries. The Cholas raised the great imperial temples of the 11th and 12th centuries, and later Pandya, Vijayanagara and Nayaka rulers expanded temple towns with vast gopurams, halls and tanks. Many of these temples remain in daily worship.

Behind the temples is a deep archaeological record: megalithic burials, Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions in rock shelters, Sangam-period towns and Roman-era trade at Arikamedu. Our guides to the Chola dynasty and Indian temple architecture give the background.

Museums in Tamil Nadu

  • Government Museum, Chennai. Famous for its Chola bronzes and Amaravati sculpture.
  • Thanjavur Art Gallery. Chola stone and bronze sculpture in the palace complex.
  • Keeladi Site Museum. Finds from the Keeladi excavations.
  • Fort Museum, Fort St George. Colonial arms, coins and portraits.

UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Tamil Nadu

The Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram (1984) includes the five rathas, the Arjuna's Penance relief, cave mandapas and the Shore Temple, mostly of the 7th and 8th centuries under the Pallavas. The Great Living Chola Temples were first listed in 1987 with the Brihadisvara temple at Thanjavur, built by Rajaraja I and completed about 1010, and extended in 2004 to include Gangaikonda Cholapuram and the Airavatesvara temple at Darasuram.

Gingee Fort in Viluppuram district is part of the Maratha Military Landscapes of India, inscribed in 2025, which covers twelve forts in Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. The Nilgiri Mountain Railway joined the Mountain Railways of India listing in 2005, and parts of the Western Ghats in Tamil Nadu fall within that natural serial site of 2012. Our programme Mamallapuram: rock-cut and structural temples is the best way to see the Pallava monuments with someone who can explain the sequence.

Ancient temples to see in Tamil Nadu

Kanchipuram has the Kailasanatha temple, an early 8th century Pallava building, along with later Ekambareshvara and Varadaraja temples. Madurai's Meenakshi temple, mostly Nayaka in its present form, is a city within a city with towering gopurams. Srirangam's Ranganatha temple is enclosed by seven concentric walls, and Chidambaram's Nataraja temple is central to the history of Shaiva worship and dance. Rameswaram's corridors and Kumbakonam's many temples add more.

Before visiting, our lecture Dravida temple architecture explains vimana, gopuram and mandapa so students can read what they see. The tour South India temple architecture links the major sites into one itinerary.

Archaeological sites: Keeladi, Adichanallur and Arikamedu

Keeladi in Sivaganga district, excavated by the ASI and then the Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology since 2015, has revealed brick structures, pottery inscribed with Tamil-Brahmi and evidence of an urban settlement of the early historic period. The dating of its earliest levels has been debated, and reports should be read with that in mind. A site museum at Keeladi displays the finds.

Adichanallur, near Tirunelveli, is a large urn-burial site of the Iron Age, first dug in the late 19th century and re-excavated recently. Arikamedu near Puducherry was a port with Roman and Mediterranean pottery from around the turn of the common era. Our lecture Burials and bioarchaeology explains what urn burials can tell us.

Forts, palaces and cities

Gingee's three hill citadels joined by walls show how successive powers, from Nayakas to Marathas, Mughals, French and British, used the same hills. Thirumalai Nayakkar Mahal in Madurai, Thanjavur's Maratha palace and Saraswathi Mahal library, Fort St George in Chennai and the Danish fort at Tharangambadi (Tranquebar) show later layers. Chettinad's mansions add a merchant community's architecture.

Our city guides cover walks in Chennai, Madurai, Thanjavur and Mahabalipuram.

Questions people ask

How many UNESCO World Heritage Sites are in Tamil Nadu?

Tamil Nadu shares in five listings: Mahabalipuram, the Great Living Chola Temples, the Maratha Military Landscapes of India (through Gingee Fort), the Mountain Railways of India (through the Nilgiri Mountain Railway) and the Western Ghats, a natural site. Only Mahabalipuram and the Chola temples lie wholly in the state.

Which temples are in the Great Living Chola Temples listing?

Three temples: the Brihadisvara temple at Thanjavur, the Brihadisvara temple at Gangaikonda Cholapuram and the Airavatesvara temple at Darasuram. They were built by Chola kings in the 11th and 12th centuries and are still in worship.

What has been found at Keeladi?

Excavations at Keeladi in Sivaganga district have found brick buildings, drains, wells, pottery with Tamil-Brahmi writing and objects pointing to an urban settlement of the early historic period. The dating of the earliest levels is debated, so read headline dates with care.

Why is Gingee Fort a UNESCO site?

Gingee is one of the twelve forts in the Maratha Military Landscapes of India, inscribed in 2025. It was held by the Marathas in the late 17th century, when Rajaram used it as a base, and shows how they adapted hill fortifications in the south.

What are the oldest temples in Tamil Nadu?

The rock-cut and structural temples of the Pallavas, from the 7th and 8th centuries, are the oldest surviving temples. Mahabalipuram's rathas and Shore Temple and the Kailasanatha temple at Kanchipuram are the best examples.
